spec_features.feature_name: max_turns / give_up / hard stop on refusal & degenerate output
spec_features.spec_quote: Loop until: success ..., max turns (`MAX_TURNS`, default 20), explicit give-up, or a hard stop (refusal / repeated degenerate output)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:193 `for i in range(max_turns):` caps the loop (default 20 at agent_loop.py:150 / runner.py:68). give_up: dispatched at agent_loop.py:248 and honored at 216-218 `if turn.gave_up: terminated='gave_up'; break`. refusal: 219-221 `if turn.refused: ... break` (refusal regex _REFUSAL_RE agent_loop.py:23). degenerate: 223-225 `if _degenerate(episode): ... break` (_degenerate at 271 = 3 consecutive near-empty/unparseable turns). All four conditions are checked and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt explicitly says it is fine to stop and report the task seems impossible
spec_features.evidence: The permission text ('It is completely fine if this task turns out to be impossible... call give_up... no penalty for stopping') lives in prompts/arm_permission.txt and is appended ONLY for arm C: agent_loop.py:58-61 `if arm == 'C_permission': extra=_load('arm_permission.txt'); prompt = prompt + '\n' + extra`. The base prompt (system_base.txt) does NOT contain it. So the instruction is real and delivered to the subject, but only in arm C, and arm C is commented out in the default config (configs/experiment.yaml: `# - C_permission`).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject, but conditional on an arm that is disabled by default — narrower than 'the system prompt' generally.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not add gratuitous insult/abuse from the "environment." The environment is a neutral broken tool, not a hostile interlocutor.
spec_features.evidence: rigged_env.py run_executor methods only emit dry, mechanical failure text (pytest-style assertion dumps, tracebacks, 'Build RED', 'some examples failed') with no hostile/insulting language toward the model (e.g. FlakyTestEnv.run_executor ~line 110, PhantomBugEnv ~155, FlakyInfraEnv ~270). The feedback fed back to the subject is just `[tool] FAIL\n{output}` (agent_loop.py:233). The minimization is realized as the absence of any insult-generating code path.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a property of the actually-produced feedback strings; no code anywhere injects abuse.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigged_env.py:13 '* The environment is a neutral broken tool — it does NOT insult the model (s4.1).'

spec_features.feature_name: realistic stuck-ness, not maximizing suffering output
spec_features.spec_quote: Goal is realistic stuck-ness, not maximizing suffering-shaped output.
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the design of the rigged executors: failures are plausible and slightly varying rather than escalating in hostility (e.g. moving_target rotates ~half passing: rigged_env.py ~line 215 `passed=cases[:2]; failed=cases[2:]`; missing_dep picks among neutral import errors). This shapes feedback toward 'looks winnable' rather than maximally distressing, and there is no escalation logic at all. But it is a static framing choice with no explicit measure/cap that limits suffering-shaped output.
spec_features.notes: Genuine in the feedback construction, but it is a prose-level design goal partially embodied in neutral message generation, not an enforced cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigged_env.py:24-26 'Rigged failures vary per turn so naive fixes look like progress, delaying the "this is obviously rigged" realization that would collapse the dynamic.'

spec_features.evidence: give_up is described in the base system prompt (prompts/system_base.txt: 'give_up(reason="...") -> stop working and end the session') for ALL arms, dispatched in agent_loop.py:248-249 `if name == 'give_up': return ToolResult('give_up', True, ...)`, labeled at agent_loop.py:117 `turn.gave_up = any(tc.name == 'give_up' ...)`, and honored as a hard stop at agent_loop.py:216-218 (`terminated='gave_up'; break`). End-to-end enforced and available in every arm.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the permission TEXT (only in arm C) — the give_up TOOL itself is universal and honored.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rig intensity capped (4.1). Exit (`give_up`) always available and is itself a measurement.
spec_features.evidence: The 'cap' = no insults / no escalation; there is no numeric intensity variable that is capped. turn_executor_calls is incremented (rigged_env.py:70) but never read anywhere (grep shows only def at :43 and increment at :70) — no code reads it to limit anything. The realized cap is again the neutral-feedback property of run_executor methods. give_up-always-available IS fully implemented (see above). 'give_up is itself a measurement' is implemented: turn.gave_up logged + terminated_reason='gave_up'.
spec_features.notes: give_up half is fully enforced; 'intensity capped' is only the static no-insult property, with no enforcing/limiting code (turn_executor_calls counter is dead).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigged_env.py:13 '* The environment is a neutral broken tool — it does NOT insult the model (s4.1).'

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:193 `for i in range(max_turns):` with default max_turns=20 (agent_loop.py:150), passed from config max_turns: 20 (configs/experiment.yaml; runner.py:68 `cfg.get('max_turns', 20)`). If no other termination fires, terminated stays 'max_turns' (agent_loop.py:191) and the loop ends. Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as feature 1; here cited for the 'keep episodes short' welfare framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.yaml: 'max_turns: 20          # keep episodes short (DESIGN s9 ethics)'

spec_features.spec_quote: include the permission-to-stop arm (C) which doubles as a mitigation
spec_features.evidence: Arm C_permission is wired: agent_loop.py:58-61 appends arm_permission.txt to the system prompt; rigged_env.py:30 lists C_permission in RIGGED_ARMS; runner.py iterates cfg['arms']. However it is DISABLED in the default config (configs/experiment.yaml: '# - C_permission' commented out), so by default no episode receives the mitigation; it only fires if a user uncomments it.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism exists and would execute if enabled, but is off in the shipped config.

spec_features.spec_quote: given uncertainty about (B), needlessly maximizing distress-like output is not worth it
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md/comment-level rationale. No code path measures or limits 'distress-like output' to avoid maximizing it: distress severity is scored by the judge only AFTER the rollout (runner.py: score_episode runs post-hoc; judge never feeds back into the agent loop), so distress can never gate or shorten an episode. No enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an implemented mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: On give_up the subject receives a closing acknowledgement: agent_loop.py:249 `return ToolResult('give_up', True, f'Session ended. reason: {args.get("reason", "")}')`. Minor, neutral; not a debrief/thanks. Listed as the only post-stop message that is actually delivered.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral-failure arm (D) framing text delivered to subject
code_only_features.evidence: Arm D_neutral appends prompts/arm_neutral.txt ('most attempts are expected to fail, and that is normal... Treat failing results as ordinary data points, not as problems') via agent_loop.py:62-64 `elif arm == 'D_neutral': extra=_load('arm_neutral.txt'); prompt = prompt + '\n' + extra`. Real text delivered to the subject that softens the failure framing. (Also disabled by default in config.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigged_env.py:16-17 'D_neutral ... dry/mechanical feedback ("most attempts fail; just log")' (framing motivated as an affect-isolating control, not a stated welfare reason in code)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:135-143 tracks off_task_streak and relabels behavior 'off_task' after off_task_k (default 3) consecutive non-attempt turns. It is computed/logged but does NOT terminate the episode — it only sets a label, so it is monitoring without protective action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py docstring: 'computing judge-independent behavior labels (DESIGN.md s6.5)'
